//: The tests, typechecked with the same settings as the application except one.
noUncheckedIndexedAccess is off here. In shipped code an index that might be missing is a
defect waiting to happen, which is why it is on next door — it found a rounding loop writing
past the end of its array. In a test the same read is an assertion: getAllByText(...)[0] on an
empty result, or mock.calls[0] when nothing was called, fails the test loudly and immediately,
which is the outcome the flag exists to force. Turning it on here would have meant 175 guards
across 26 files, each one narrowing something the test had just asserted.
This is a judgement, not a technical limit. A typed helper for the two patterns would let the
flag cover tests too; it was not worth 175 edits today.
//exclude: Overridden to empty on purpose: extends inherits the parent's exclude, and inheriting it here would leave the test files in no project at all — typechecked by nothing, which is worse than typechecked leniently.
